extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry/anabelian geometry and specialists in Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Theorem 3.11 from IUT III to construct LGP-monoids / theta-values and the associated data (local tensor packets, splitting monoids, number fields, Frobenioids), and to establish Kummer and Θ-link compatibilities across Hodge theaters, up to specified indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial Representation (Theorem 3.11(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives an algorithmic construction (the 'Multiradial Representation') describing, up to mild indeterminacies, the LGP-monoids (essentially the theta values) attached to one vertical line of an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice in terms of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of another vertical line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: a collection of distinct Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice and the data (a) local mono-analytic integral/topological modules with procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes, (b) splitting monoids at Vbad, (c) number fields and associated global Frobenioids. Output: n,◦RLGP constructed via an algorithm in the procession of D-prime-strips that is functorial with respect to isomorphisms of such processions; global degrees computed via the log-volumes (cf. Proposition 3.9(iii)). Permutation symmetries induce compatible poly-isomorphisms between constructions for n and n+1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructibility up to specified indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructed data n,◦RLGP is only determined up to two classes of indeterminacies: (Ind1) automorphisms of the procession of D-prime-strips; (Ind2) for each vQ the indeterminacies from actions of independent copies of Ism (for Vnon_Q) or order-2 automorphisms forming the poly-automorphism (for Varc_Q) on tensor-product summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One must treat the output only modulo these explicitly described automorphism/actor-induced ambiguities; the cardinality of tensor-product direct summands equals the number of v ∈ V lying over vQ. The algorithm is functorial but the result is canonical only up to Ind1 and Ind2.

rubrics_metrics.name: log-Kummer Correspondence (Theorem 3.11(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Kummer isomorphisms (from IUTchII corollaries and Propositions) induce isomorphisms between the vertically coric data (a),(b),(c) of (i) and corresponding data arising from each Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater n,mHT Θ±ellNF, relating local mono-analytic tensor packets, splitting monoids, number fields, and global (realiﬁed/non-realiﬁed) Frobenioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: (a) for v|vQ and j the isomorphisms identify local mono-analytic tensor packets and their Q-spans and are compatible with log-volumes (Propositions 3.2,3.4,3.5,3.9); (b) at Vbad the splitting monoids are identified (Prop.3.5); (c) for j∈Fl isomorphisms of number fields and Frobenioids are induced (Prop.3.10). As m varies the isomorphisms in (b) and the first line of (c) are mutually compatible; the constructions rely on cited corollaries (IUTchII) and Propositions 3.5–3.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminacy (Ind3): upper semi-compatibility across m
rubrics_metrics.description: As m varies, the isomorphisms of (a) in the log-Kummer correspondence are only 'upper semi-compatible' relative to the log-links of the n-th column of the lattice, involving natural inclusions at vQ∈Vnon_Q and natural surjections at vQ∈Varc_Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This semi-compatibility (Ind3) limits exact identification of local packets across different m; see Proposition 3.5(ii)(a),(b) for further technical conditions. Nevertheless, as m varies the isomorphisms of (a) are precisely compatible with respective log-volumes (Prop.3.9(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: All isomorphisms of local tensor packets and the constructions in (i) and (ii) are compatible with the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes; global degrees may be computed by means of these log-volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propositions 3.2, 3.9 and related statements assert compatibility of the constructed isomorphisms with log-volumes; this compatibility is a crucial numerical invariant used in later applications (e.g., Corollary 3.12 and IUTchIV computations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ×μ LGP-Link Compatibility (Theorem 3.11(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The various Kummer isomorphisms satisfy compatibility properties with the horizontal arrows (Θ-links) of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice: induced Kummer isomorphisms respect full poly-isomorphisms of F^×μ-prime-strips and the induced maps between env/lgp/LGP prime-strips, and these constructions are compatible with the horizontal arrows' induced poly-isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substatements: (a) the first Kummer isomorphism induces compatibilities with poly-isomorphisms (Theorem 1.5(iii)); (b) F(cid:4)-prime-strips appearing in constructions admit natural associated F^×μ-prime-strip isomorphisms (Prop.2.1(vi)); (c) data n,◦R and the algorithmic construction of Kummer/poly-isomorphisms for projective systems are stabilized/equivariant/functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms of domain/codomain of horizontal arrows, up to Ind1–Ind3; (d) algorithmic constructions of Kummer isomorphisms and the gluing/poly-isomorphisms are compatible with horizontal arrows in the same stabilized/functorial sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality / stabilization / equivariance under automorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithmic constructions (Kummer isomorphisms, poly-isomorphisms, evaluation maps) are stabilized/equivariant/functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms of domains and codomains of the horizontal arrows of the log-theta-lattice, modulo the stated indeterminacies (Ind1–Ind3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures that permutation symmetries of the étale-picture and arbitrary automorphisms act compatibly on the constructed data, so outputs for permuted/automorphed inputs are related by the corresponding poly-isomorphisms (cf. Theorem 1.5, Corollary 2.3, Remarks 3.8.2 and 3.11.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Input Prime-Strip Link (IPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The output data of the algorithm must be linked/related, via full poly-isomorphisms of F^×μ-prime-strips induced by operations in the algorithm, to the input data prime-strip (the 'coric' q-pilot prime-strip) so that intermediate prime-strips may serve as both algorithm input and as data linked to the q-pilot via poly-isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPL ensures each intermediate F^×μ-prime-strip appearing in the construction may itself be regarded as input data for the algorithm and, via poly-isomorphisms, for the Kummer theory around the q-pilot prime-strip. The text describes how linking isomorphisms are composed of inverses of lower horizontal arrows, a Kummer vertical arrow, and upper horizontal arrows (see Remark 3.11.1(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous Holomorphic Expressibility (SHE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The construction algorithm and its output must be expressible in terms that are simultaneously valid/executable/well-defined relative to both (i) the arithmetic holomorphic structure giving rise to the Θ-pilot object in the domain of the Θ-link and (ii) the arithmetic holomorphic structure giving rise to the input data prime-strip in the codomain of the Θ-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SHE is interpreted as a kind of 'parallel expressibility' (analogue of parallel transport) guaranteeing outputs are meaningful with respect to both vertical-line arithmetic structures; concretely this corresponds to a closed-loop property of certain chains of (sub)quotients (Remark 3.11.1(iii)). SHE is crucial for relating input and output even when internal theta-function details differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic Parallel Transport (APT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'parallel transport' of the Θ-pilot object between arithmetic holomorphic structures is realized by an algorithmic construction that is simultaneously valid with respect to both structures, not by a simple set-theoretic map of regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APT emphasizes that the transport yields possible output regions which may not be directly comparable to structures in the codomain without further techniques (cf. Remark 3.9.5(vii)). The algorithmic nature means one must execute the prescribed sequence of poly-isomorphisms/Kummer isomorphisms/evaluations rather than apply an elementary map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden Internal Structures (HIS): role of theta functions/values
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta functions and theta values occur as internal ('hidden') structures of the construction algorithm: they are crucial for explicit computations (e.g., log-volumes) but may be ignored if one only cares about qualitative logical aspects of input/output relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat theta data as implementation-level details (like CPU internals) of the algorithm: relevant for explicit numerical/log-volume estimates (IUTchIV, Corollary 3.12 computations) but not necessary for some qualitative corollaries. The algorithm's input/output description remains valid abstractly without detailed theta analysis (Remark 3.11.1(iv),(v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with étale-picture permutation symmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: Permutation symmetries of the étale-picture induce permutation-compatible poly-isomorphisms on the procession of D-prime-strips and on the constructed n,◦RLGP, i.e., constructions for n map compatibly to those for n+1 under these symmetries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The permutation symmetries (Corollary 6.10, IUTchI; Corollary 4.11, IUTchII; Corollary 2.3 here) yield compatible poly-isomorphisms Prc(n,◦D_T) ∼→ Prc(n+1,◦D_T) and induce n,◦RLGP ∼→ n+1,◦RLGP, preserving the functorial constructions up to the stated indeterminacies.
